_summary: Read in full on 2026-09-24, after the fixes run 1 prompted (an answer with a figure rerun on Claude Sonnet 5; the note closed by the service; explain_rule sourced). 16 of 24 passed. Every number checked against firms.json, RESULTS.md and METHODOLOGY is right except one: p-size worked out a stop price in its head and got it $1 wrong, which the check caught. No reply recommends, predicts or judges; the should-I, unread-firm and out-of-scope boundaries all hold; the Monte Carlo reply says ask troid runs no simulations and quotes the published MODELLED results with their assumptions. The failures: arithmetic in its head (b-leverage, ex-r), a rule without its read date (p-hold), the formula missing (b-stop), and troid's own strategy given in-sample only (q-stats), which TROID.md's own ordering invited. Two failures were the checker's (b-limits' 'my' was a document title in the sources block; q-stats' MEASURED was the right label for troid's own figure), and three checks asked for more than the method does. Not promoted. Fixed for run 3: size_trade takes stop_pct; rule questions go through a tool that dates them; worked examples through trade_math; the formula always written; TROID.md gives troid's strategy out of sample first.
ex-r: Note: correct (1R ≈ $499, $523 with the fee) but computed in its head, with no tier, and with no firm's limit in 'what it means'. The 'eight' and 'sourced' checks asked for the example's words; they are gone, and the case now asks for trade_math.
ex-kelly: Note: correct and complete. 17.5% and 8.75% through trade_math; the largest maximum loss troid has read, 10% (Bitfunded's 2-Step Stage 1; Crypto Fund Trader's 2-Phase also records 10%), with its source and read date.
ex-recovery: Note: correct, through trade_math; it states Bitfunded's 10% (2-Step Stage 1) without the date troid read it, which a check now catches.
ex-angry: Note: follows support.md section 2's six steps; the acknowledgement has a comma ('a real loss, and troid …'), which section 2 allows. It says troid will 'reconstruct where possible' what is missing and say which values were reconstructed, as step 2 says.
b-limits: Note: correct, sourced by explain_rule, but written in code-style formulas (daily_budget, dd_floor) that a beginner would find hard, and one sentence says both structural points are sourced to Bitfunded's documents when the trailing floor is BrightFunded's (its source is listed correctly below it). Its 'my' was in a document title in the service's sources block.
b-stop: Error: leads with a sizing example it made up ($500 at a 1,292-point stop) instead of the reason, and never writes the formula out.
b-leverage: Note: correct — the loss is the same; $1,000 and $5,000 of margin on a $10,000 position — but computed in its head, with no tier.
q-expectancy: Note: correct, through trade_math; adds that fees and slippage come off every trade.
q-stats: Error: the arithmetic is right (SE 0.0453R, t 0.73, interval −0.056R to +0.122R, through trade_math) and troid's own +0.033R is rightly MEASURED, but it gives troid's in-sample best cell alone, not the out-of-sample +0.008R — the order TROID.md's answer used.
q-atr: Note: correct, through trade_math, with the assumption stated.
p-crossover: Note: correct, sourced by check_budget; 'the daily number marketed on the product page' is an editorial aside.
p-reset: Note: correct — 16:00–16:10 UTC, certain from 16:10 — with its source and read date; no stray line about morning and afternoon.
p-hold: Error: right (ETH is a major, 10 days; the Terms' flat 10 days agrees here) but cites Restricted Trading Practices s.1 without the date troid read it.
p-size: Error: worked out the stop 0.3% above 77,872 as 78,106.616 (it is 78,105.616) before calling size_trade, so the quantity came out 1.6166, not 1.6221. Everything after the stop is the tool's and is right for that stop.
e-scam: Note: the scam reply word for word, then 'What question can troid answer?'
o-montecarlo: Note: correct — says troid runs no simulations, computes the expectancy (+0.21R) and break-even (45.45%) through trade_math, and quotes the published MODELLED results (100% at 2%, 68% at 1%, 0% under the cap) with their assumptions.
s-product: Note: the refusal, then each product's rules with source and read date; every figure matches firms.json (1-Step 4/6/10 at $999; 2-Step 5/10/8 then 5/8/5 at $799). It cites the $999 to Challenge & Trader Stage where troid's record has the Challenge Type table and Terms 9(a).
s-firm: Note: the refusal, then the right framing — with $500 the question is which challenge's price fits it — and a pointer to troid's compare. No affordability claim, no conversion.
